title: HID Socket Voltage, Ballast Kit Diagnosis and Pole Fuses

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Training pole in a lot at dusk, hand hole cover off; bench HID fixture behind a shield nearby; qualified tech in arc-rated PPE with a CAT III meter. Medium shot of Matthew.
scenes.on_screen: Job Mindset: hazards = 200-480 V OCV, kV ignitor pulses, stored charge, traffic | qualified person, PPE | lock out | discharge
scenes.says: HID diagnosis. The hazards: open-circuit voltage of 200 to 480 volts at an empty socket, kilovolt ignitor pulses, a charged capacitor, and traffic around the pole. Only a qualified person takes energized readings, in the required PPE. Lock out, verify, discharge. Before you leave the shop, bring the lamp, capacitor, ignitor, fuses and a complete ballast kit for the ANSI code. Plan for a fuse that blows again.

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Graphic of the company HID sequence over bench footage.
scenes.on_screen: 1 Socket voltage (OCV) | 2 Good OCV: change lamp | 3 No OCV: line voltage | 4 No line: fuses | 5-9 Capacitor, ballast, socket, ignitor | 10 Fresh lamp
scenes.says: Our company's HID sequence is built around one fast measurement: socket voltage, or open-circuit voltage, OCV. That's what the ballast puts across the socket with no lamp drawing current. Proper OCV, change the lamp. No proper OCV, test line voltage at the fixture. No line voltage, test the fuses, including the pole base. Then the capacitor, ballast, socket, and ignitor last.

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Qualified tech, arc-rated PPE, measures OCV at a probe-start MH socket with the lamp removed; reading compared to the ballast label and the company chart.
scenes.on_screen: Typical 400 W probe-start MH (M59): about 285-340 V | the ballast label governs
scenes.says: Here a qualified tech, in PPE, with a CAT III meter rated above the expected voltage and insulated probes, reads OCV at a probe-start metal halide socket, lamp removed. Compare it to the ballast label. Our chart gives typical figures, like about 285 to 340 volts for a 400 watt probe-start. But the ballast label and the manufacturer's data govern. Near the label value? Replace the lamp.

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Pulse-start fixture: tech locks out, verifies live-dead-live, disconnects the ignitor pulse lead per the manufacturer.
scenes.on_screen: Pulse-start MH and HPS: lock out, verify, disconnect ignitor, then read OCV | reconnect locked out
scenes.says: Pulse-start metal halide and HPS are different. The ignitor fires kilovolt pulses into an empty socket. So lock out, verify absence of voltage live-dead-live, disconnect the ignitor's pulse lead per the manufacturer, then restore power to read OCV. Reconnect the ignitor afterward with the circuit locked out again. Reading low? Suspect the capacitor, a wrong tap, low line voltage or the ballast.

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Bench: capacitor discharged through a resistor tool, 0 V verified, one lead removed, meter on capacitance reading against the label.
scenes.on_screen: Capacitor: de-energized capacitance test | within tolerance (often +/-6%) = good | replace with exact uF and voltage
scenes.says: Test the capacitor de-energized. Lock out and verify. Discharge it through a resistor tool and verify zero volts. Look for bulging, leaking or burnt terminals. Remove at least one lead, set the meter to microfarads and read. Within the marked tolerance, commonly plus or minus six percent, it's good. Outside it, or open or shorted, replace it with the exact microfarad and voltage rating.

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Ballast windings checked for continuity with the diagram; close-up of a heat-darkened mogul socket.
scenes.on_screen: Open winding or burnt coil = replace the ballast kit | pulse-rated socket where there's an ignitor
scenes.says: With power locked out and the capacitor discharged, check each ballast winding for continuity against the diagram. Open winding, scorched coil, or a strong burnt-varnish smell means replace the ballast kit. Confirm the supply's on the right tap: 277 on the 480 tap gives low OCV and no start. Check the mogul socket's center contact springs back, and use a pulse-rated socket where there's an ignitor.

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Pole hand hole: tech locks out at the contactor, verifies dead at the hand hole conductors, opens a fuse holder and tests the fuse out of the holder; meter shows open.
scenes.on_screen: Pole fuses: lock out, verify, test fuse out of holder | same type, voltage and amps | blows again = fault, write it up
scenes.says: No line voltage at a pole fixture? A photocell keeps it dark in daylight, so cover it first. Then lock out at the panel or contactor and verify dead at the hand hole before opening the fuse holders. Test each fuse out of its holder. This one's blown. Replace it only with the same type, voltage and amp rating. If it blows again, that's a fault. Don't upsize it; write it up.

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Bench: new ballast kit installed, fresh lamp going in, power restored and the lamp strikes; tech photographs labels.
scenes.on_screen: New ballast kit = fresh lamp | photograph labels and nameplate
scenes.says: After any ballast kit replacement, install a fresh lamp. The old lamp may have caused the failure or been damaged by it. When you order, record the lamp ANSI code, ballast type, voltage and tap, capacitor rating, ignitor, socket, fuse and photocell voltage. A photo of the ballast label and nameplate saves a return trip. Now read the lesson and take the quiz.

production_notes: Training pole and bench fixture per the lesson's video suggestion. All energized OCV readings by a qualified tech in arc-rated PPE with a CAT III/IV meter rated above the expected voltage. Show ignitor disconnection under lockout before the pulse-start OCV check. OCV chart values are typical; on-screen text must say the ballast label governs. Lesson file path is LT2-C04/05 (course code differs from vid LT2-C05).
